question: Should OpenClaw accept node-scoped clients publishing agent-visible plugin/MCP tools through node.pluginTools.update once the API compatibility blockers are fixed?
rationale: This changes which connected-node capabilities become model-visible executable tools, so automation can identify narrow repairs but cannot choose the permanent product and trust boundary.

options.title: Accept after API repairs
options.body: Keep node.pluginTools.update as the runtime publication path, repair Swift and GatewayClient compatibility, refresh the branch, and then land if maintainers accept the trust model.

options.title: Narrow the public API
options.body: Remove the wrapper connect-time option and document node-host publication as an OpenClaw node runtime path until maintainers define a broader external client contract.

options.title: Pause for protocol design
options.body: Defer this PR if maintainers want a separate design for descriptor provenance, node identity, allow/deny matching, and node-to-model execution policy.

recommendation.title: Accept after API repairs
recommendation.body: Keep node.pluginTools.update as the runtime publication path, repair Swift and GatewayClient compatibility, refresh the branch, and then land if maintainers accept the trust model.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current history on plugin-tool and Gateway/node-adjacent surfaces and owns this PR's candidate implementation path.
